title: Spawn-time slash-command resolution drops the arguments after the command, so a /review-code delegation reviews an empty tree
outcome: Spawn-time slash-command resolution drops the arguments after the command, so a /review-code delegation reviews an empty tree
acceptance: When termal_spawn_session receives a prompt that starts with a resolvable slash command followed by arguments (for example a commit range or a brief path), the arguments are preserved and passed to the command the same way /review-changes ARGUMENTS are; or the spawn is refused with a typed error, never silently truncated
A test spawns a reviewer with '/review-code <range> <brief path>' and asserts that the child prompt contains the arguments, or that a typed refusal is returned
disposal_reason: Same argument-loss behaviour, found again in a live review on 2026-11-09 and being fixed under w-941e0fdc6e2f with the broader no-input protocol line. Its holder is to check this item's criteria at closing, per Sol-a7bb mailbox f59d4581 #2862; this item's original observations stay here for reference.
